title: Best Polynomial-Time Approximation for Restricted Santa Claus
short_statement: Restricted Santa Claus has a $4+\delta$ polynomial-time algorithm and an existential configuration-LP bound $53/15$; close the constructive gap.
open_problem: Determine the best polynomial-time approximation ratio for restricted max-min fair allocation, and in particular close the gap between the $4+\delta$ algorithm and the $53/15$ configuration-LP existence bound.
background: The restricted Santa Claus problem has two related but distinct open questions. One asks for the integrality gap of the configuration LP; the other asks for the best polynomial-time approximation algorithm. These are not the same because the strongest LP-gap proofs rely on local-search or hypergraph-matching arguments whose polynomial-time convergence is difficult. The best current polynomial-time guarantee is Cheng and Mao's $4+\delta$ approximation. Their same work improved the LP integrality-gap upper bound to about $3.808$; Haxell and Szabo subsequently reached $53/15$, showing that better allocations exist relative to the LP than current efficient algorithms can necessarily find. The open problem is to close this constructive-versus-existential gap.
full_statement: Given players $P$, resources $R$, resource values $v_r$, and desire sets $R_p\subseteq R$, find a polynomial-time algorithm that allocates every resource to at most one player and maximizes, up to approximation, $\min_{p\in P}\sum_{r\in A_p\cap R_p}v_r$. The restricted case means every acceptable resource has the same value $v_r$ for all players who desire it; unacceptable resources have value $0$. Let $OPT$ be the maximum possible minimum bundle value. Determine the infimum constant $\alpha$ for which there is a polynomial-time $\alpha$-approximation for all restricted instances. In particular, can one beat the current $4+\delta$ polynomial-time guarantee, match the best known configuration-LP existence bound $53/15$, or prove that no polynomial-time algorithm below some larger threshold exists under standard complexity assumptions?
known_results: Feige and Asadpour-Feige-Saberi established constant-factor existence results for restricted max-min allocation through configuration-LP and hypergraph-matching methods. Annamalai, Kalaitzis, and Svensson gave a polynomial-time $13$-approximation, introducing lazy updates and other devices to make local search terminate efficiently. Cheng and Mao subsequently improved polynomial-time guarantees, first to $6+\delta$ and then to $4+\delta$ for every fixed $\delta>0$; their 2019 paper also proves the stronger existential configuration-LP integrality-gap upper bound $3+21/26\approx3.808$. The lower-bound side includes the basic hardness barrier of factor $2$ for related max-min allocation formulations and the known configuration-LP lower bound of $2$. The remaining open problem is the constructive threshold: whether the $4+\delta$ algorithm can be improved, whether the newer $53/15$ existence bound can be made algorithmic, or whether a new hardness or algorithmic barrier separates efficient algorithms from the LP gap. Haxell and Szabo (SODA 2023; Combinatorica 2025), Theorem 1.1, improve the restricted configuration-LP gap to $53/15$. This is existential, not a polynomial-time allocation algorithm.

progress.summary: The polynomial-time guarantee remains $4+\delta$; the stronger existential LP-gap bound is $53/15$.

counterexample_rationale: Finite instances can expose failures of candidate local-search algorithms, but approximation lower bounds require reductions.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search can stress local-search rules and identify slow-convergence or hard allocation hypergraphs. Algorithmic progress needs proof of polynomial convergence and approximation ratio.

literature.synthesis: The algorithmic history tracks the effort to make hypergraph-matching-style existence proofs efficient. Purely combinatorial local search brought the first usable polynomial constants, and Cheng-Mao's refinements reduced the ratio to $4+\delta$. The remaining gap to the $53/15$ integrality bound may be an artifact of analysis, a real barrier for known local-search algorithms, or a sign that a different rounding method is needed. Any improvement must preserve polynomial running time, not just show that a good allocation exists.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Study whether Cheng-Mao local search can be sharpened to match the $53/15$ existential LP bound, or whether alternative hypergraph matching algorithms yield better constructive ratios.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: Do not confuse an integrality-gap proof with a polynomial-time approximation algorithm. A claimed algorithmic improvement must output an actual allocation, run in time polynomial in the input size for every fixed accuracy parameter, and compare its value with the true optimum or a clearly stated LP upper bound. If the proof uses augmenting trees, hypergraph matchings, or blocker sequences, the referee should check both the approximation invariant and the polynomial bound on the number of local-search steps. A hardness claim must specify whether it is for restricted valuations and whether the threshold is relative to $OPT$ rather than to the configuration LP.
